Conjecture 1. If G is a Šoltés graph, then G is regular.

    For a general regular graph G, the values W (G−u) and W (G−v) might be signiﬁcantly
diﬀerent for two diﬀerent vertices u, v ∈ V (G); it may happen that removal of one vertex
increases the Wiener index, while removal of the other vertex descreases the Wiener index.
However, W (G − u) and W (G − v) are equal if vertices u and v belong to the same vertex
orbit. Therefore, we believe that a Šoltés graph is likely to be vertex transitive.

Conjecture 2. If G is a Šoltés graph, then G is vertex transitive.

    Among truncations of cubic vertex-transitive graphs we found several 31 -Šoltés graphs;
see Section 4. Interestingly, all our examples are in fact Cayley graphs and this leads us
to pose the following conjecture.

Conjecture 3. If G is a Šoltés graph, then G is a Cayley graph.
